- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.  
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.25) and price is trending down, model often underestimates fall; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.  
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon; apply 2–5% downward adjustment for first 7–10 days.  
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore it; apply 1–3% upward bias to counteract.  
- When sentiment is high and price is near support level, model often fails to recognize reversal; add 1–2% downward buffer to prevent overbought overcorrection.
